steps.name: Sarkaz Civilian
steps.text: Look! Up ahead!

steps.name: Sarkaz Civilian
steps.text: The bridge... it's been blown? How are we supposed to get across?

steps.name: Sarkaz Civilian
steps.text: I-Is there another path? The Catastrophe cloud is still over our heads...

steps.name: Sarkaz Civilian
steps.text: We can't go any further, not with all the wounded and children...

steps.name: Babel Member
steps.text: Damn, the Originium crystals on the ground are starting to glow...

steps.name: Babel Member
steps.text: They'll kill us before the Catastrophe even has a chance.

steps.name: Babel Member
steps.text: *cough*

steps.name: Babel Member
steps.text: We need to—

steps.name: Babel Member
steps.text: *cough*—

steps.name: Babel Member
steps.text: *cough* *cough*—

steps.name: Babel Member
steps.text: We need to go... It's all *Sarkaz expletive* Originium particles in the air.

steps.name: Babel Member
steps.text: No medicine for more than a week now... all the injured... Infected... damn it!

steps.name: Babel Member
steps.text: Wh-What's that sound?

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: No reinforcements from Babel yet? Then keep looking for a path! Don't come back until you do!

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: The Catastrophe cloud's fully formed. Which *Sarkaz expletive* unit attacked the hospital? Not even Scareye's that crazy!

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Stick together! It's too late to try to get out of the Catastrophe. We need to find some clean caves! Nothing with Originium traces on it, not even a little bit!

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Doing this to the wounded... Theresis, you piece of...

steps.name: Sarkaz Child
steps.text: Mom... my leg hurts...

steps.name: Sarkaz Civilian
steps.text: Don't cry, don't cry... we're almost home...

steps.name: Sarkaz Child
steps.text: No— no—

steps.name: Sarkaz Child
steps.text: It hurts— It hurts...
The sound of children crying.
The sound of conspiracy, of death, of struggling to survive.
The Catastrophe is deaf to all that, turning wind and snow into storm.
A few figures stand on a distant cliff.
The woman stands on the edge, peering silently into the distance.
A merciless Catastrophe, enemy soldiers blocking key passages, fleeing beasts, and the wounded and civilians with nowhere to run.
Life echoes in the valley, reaching Mantra's ears.
It is the sound of children crying.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: ...I hear it.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: Children are crying.

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: It's starting to snow. This isn't good.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: Two thousand, three hundred and thirteen.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: All confirmed.

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: Location and physical data logged.

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: Fewer losses than expected, but time's of the essence.

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: Watching your Arts up close is always a remarkable experience, Mantra.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: (Nods humbly)

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: Was the Djall in HR able to get you a few assistants?

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: (Closes eyes)

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: A shame.

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: Message sent to all squads.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: Cave, seven kilometers to the northeast.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: The children are there.

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: But the Military Commission's drones have found us.

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: I'll stay. You go.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: (Frowns)

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: They don't want to face my squad head-on in this terrain.

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: Just going to say hi. Will try to take Manfred alive if he's leading them.

steps.name: Mantra
steps.text: Don't take unnecessary risks—

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Doctor here.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Sorry I'm late. Operations in the CA area have concluded.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Continue to carry out Mantra's plan. I'll provide support elsewhere. The priority is to help the civilians and wounded.

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: Good timing, Doctor.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Thanks. Misery is distracting the Military Commission, but he needs help.

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: Is this the part where I volunteer?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Yes, Ace.

steps.name: Ace
steps.text: Awaiting your orders.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: And...

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Theresa will go directly to the affected field hospital at the center to prevent further casualties.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: If all goes well... I'll meet you there.

steps.name: Babel Member
steps.text: Explosion! Explosion!

steps.name: Babel Member
steps.text: Move away from the glowing area! Back off! The Originium underground is being activated—

steps.name: Babel Member
steps.text: *Sarkaz expletive* Too late—
Fires stir beneath the frozen earth, and blizzard brings with it the sparks of Catastrophe.
Every breath seems to carry the weight of all of Terra, bringing it upon every individual soul.
The weight vanishes in an instant.
They look up to see an astonishing sight.

steps.name: Babel Member
steps.text: Gah—

steps.name: Babel Member
steps.text: ...The explosions stopped?

steps.name: Babel Member
steps.text: Snow... floating in the air?

steps.name: Pith
steps.text: The snow crystals here are almost indistinguishable from Originium crystals. Control over them can be achieved with sufficient focus.

steps.name: Babel Member
steps.text: You... You're

steps.name: Pith
steps.text: Precise control over individual snowflakes is difficult, but it's not so difficult to hold a snowstorm off in an Originium-rich environment.

steps.name: Pith
steps.text: Have you been paying attention in class, Aidan?

steps.name: Babel Member
steps.text: Pith! You're here! You...

steps.name: Pith
steps.text: I can give you ten minutes.

steps.name: Pith
steps.text: Go back to the meadows at the bottom of the valley and head south. Scout will guide your path.

steps.name: Pith
steps.text: Don't you remember what I taught you? There are a lot of emergency precautions you can take in an Originium-dense environment, but you did nothing.

steps.name: Babel Member
steps.text: I—

steps.name: Pith
steps.text: Wait... you have acute Oripathy patients in your group! What were you thinking?!

steps.name: Pith
steps.text: Take this syringe! I'll do what I can. You have ten minutes to get everybody in order.

steps.name: Babel Member
steps.text: But you—

steps.name: Pith
steps.text: Move it, before the Catastrophe fully forms! This area will be safe while I can dampen it for a bit.

steps.name: Pith
steps.text: —One more thing.

steps.name: Pith
steps.text: I'm using several kinds of Arts at the same time right now. I want to see an essay from all of you on my table by this weekend, explaining which schools these Arts belong to.

steps.name: Pith
steps.text: So you better damn well make it out alive.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary A
steps.text: ...It's me. Any instructions from Manfred?

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary A
steps.text: What is he doing? Huh?

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary A
steps.text: A Royal Court high rank in amongst the Babel forces and refugees? Impossible! Look it up!

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary B
steps.text: Doubt there's anything to look up. Manfred probably made up the excuse on the spot.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary B
steps.text: Even if they were there, they're Babel prisoners now. Rescuing prisoners in the middle of a Catastrophe is not part of the contract.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary A
steps.text: But we have to do it anyway. Dammit, get Thorn Squad to check the blockade...

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary B
steps.text: Alright... 86 here. Hello? Hello?

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary B
steps.text: No response. Where did they go? It's not time for the shift change yet, is it?

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary B
steps.text: ...Wait.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary B
steps.text: Isn't it a little too quiet?

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary B
steps.text: There were fowlbeast cries only a moment ago...

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary A
steps.text: All the animals must have fled the Catastrophe.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary A
steps.text: It'll sweep through this place in five hours. This is no time to be taking a nap.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary A
steps.text: Hand me the schedule.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary A
steps.text: I said, hand me the—

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary A
steps.text: Huh? Hey, where did you go?

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary A
steps.text: Hello? This is Squad 86! Anyone hear me? Anybody? What's going on? Somebody's—

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: You called?

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: Phew.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: Three squads silenced. No alerts. The path is clear.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: Combat personnel, follow these coordinates. Medics, take the injured and follow the markings I've left.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: ...There's something I need to confirm.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: It's the Military Commission's frequency alright, but these were scouts, not the rogue mercenaries that attacked our positions.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: Mission briefing 'Strawberry'. Just monitoring the retreat of the civilians... hah, Manfred even lied to them that there was a 'Royal Court high rank' here.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: Well, I guess I'll leave the rest to Ascalon.

steps.name: Mysterious Mercenary
steps.text: Babel.

steps.name: Mysterious Mercenary
steps.text: Are you my death?

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: You led the attack on Babel positions. Who's orders are you following?

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: It's just doctors and Infected civilians—
The sword comes before she can finish her sentence.
Something feels out of place.
But Ascalon adjusts quickly. She has always been more familiar with the language of violence anyway.
The sleeve-blade is out of its sheath.

steps.name: Mysterious Mercenary
steps.text: Ngh.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: What are you—

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Bomb... you're crazy.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Surrender. You have no chan—

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: ...It's me. I'm done.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Sorry, couldn't take him alive. He blew himself up.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Something's not right.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: He recognized me as Babel immediately, realized he was no match for me and quickly chose to blow himself up.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Abnormally decisive. Could be some experienced spy, or...

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Wait.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: I found a pouch. It's undamaged. I must have cut it off.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: There's a Babel sleeve badge and a Military Commission medal inside.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: It's not unusual for a mercenary working both sides of a war.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: And a piece of paper. Possibly personal notes.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Most of it is illegible. The only thing I can make out is...

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: '...del. Home.'

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Forget it. Not important.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Communications are out? Well, I guess the old stuff won't do it when a Catastrophe is so close.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Let's hope the other teams found a way out.

steps.name: Julie
steps.text: Don't just stand there.

steps.name: Julie
steps.text: Bring all the Infected who can't move over here.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: What's the point? It's not like they'll be able to get away from the Catastrophe.

steps.name: Julie
steps.text: Just do it. It's not like you have anything to lose, is there?

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: And...? Some of them are comatose.

steps.name: Julie
steps.text: My condition isn't that far off from theirs. I'll end their suffering.

steps.name: Julie
steps.text: Originium particles will spread when they die. I'll take the brunt of it. Take your bow, keep your distance, and finish the job.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: (Mumbles) Hell no.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Hey, stay away from the Infected. Julie will deal with them.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: ...Infected.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: You're just leaving them here like firewood.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: I'm not doing it because I want to.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Is there any hope for them?

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: No. Just death. They'll turn to dust in ten minutes or so.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: They could have been saved.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Does living a little longer count as being saved?

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Their conditions are too severe. If they don't die here, they'll die in some forgotten alleyway in Kazdel. I should have stayed in Sargon...

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Here, give them these suppressants. It'll at least relieve their pain.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Where did you get these suppressants? No, who are you anyway? When did you get here?

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Don't move!

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Your ID code, now, or I'll—
Let the Doctor pass.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: It's fine.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Everything will be fine.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: You look familiar—

steps.name: Julie
steps.text: Y-Your Highness! How could you—

steps.name: Julie
steps.text: We're right in the middle of the Catastrophe! W-We're very grateful, but...

steps.name: Julie
steps.text: You shouldn't have come! It's too dangerous—
The white Sarkaz appears on the battlefield without a sound, as though she has come out of nowhere.
The crowd whispers amongst themselves. Is she truly the King of Babel, one of the living Six Heroes, the mother of Kazdel?
Theresa simply nods at confused and bewildered crowd.
She kneels by the side of the Infected.

steps.name: Dying Infected
steps.text: Your... Highness...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I'm sorry I came late.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Too late to save your lives... I'm sorry I couldn't do enough...

steps.name: Dying Infected
steps.text: Please... don't...
Theresa gently holds his hand in hers.
The other Infected, all the ones still conscious, those who have not fully given up on living, feel a little bit of gentle warmth.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I'm listening, my children.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I will remember how all of you lived and died... forgive me that I could not promise you more, but for your family, children, friends and comrades...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: There will come a day when they will no longer live in fear.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Your lives should have been so much more.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Now, though, dream a warm dream... a dream that will come true.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Sleep, children of Kazdel. Sleep in the warm embrace of home.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Sleep.

steps.name: Dying Infected
steps.text: Thank... you...
The Infected begin to glow with the colors of Originium.
Tiny stones eat away at flesh and blood, transforming their lives and desires into fleeting sparks.
Theresa holds their hands to the end.
Until shining dust rises towards the sky and is scattered by the wind, never to become stars upon the heavens.

steps.name: Julie
steps.text: So, you... er...

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: You can call me anything you like. Even 'evil spirit', if that's what you prefer.

steps.name: Julie
steps.text: I-I don't mean that! It's just, this is the first time we've spoken to each other alone.

steps.name: Julie
steps.text: You brought us many victories. I've had a hand in some. They also say you're an expert on Originium...

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: ...'Expert'.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Yet it's the first time I've seen Infected die like this with my own two eyes.

steps.name: Julie
steps.text: You're lucky.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I never thought it would be so...

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Does living a little longer count as being saved?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: ...Never mind.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: It's time to go, Theresa.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Right.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: But it's too late, even if we leave now. And the Military Commission has set a trap for us...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: It'll be fine.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Let's go home.
The Military Commission's after-action report writes:
'The King of Babel and her most trusted men led her people out of the valley.
'With a single touch she parted wind, snow, and flames, gentle as a mother parts the bed curtains to put her child to sleep.
'Our casters and crossbowmen observed the procession, but none dared take the first shot, nor give the order to.'
The flowery report and Manfred's 'false intelligence' earned an admonition from the Commission, but no further discipline.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Doctor.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I heard about the operation. You...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Doctor?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: There's something I want to ask, Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Go ahead.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: As a physician, is it saving a life when all you can do is stave off death for a little while?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Unless it goes contrary to the patient's wishes, the duty of a physician is to save lives.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: That's what we've always worked to do.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Why do you ask?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Looking at Amiya and the people around us makes me feel that you shouldn't have to deal with this kind of suffering.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: And I...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Doctor, Kal'tsit, there you are.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: The intelligence meeting just ended. The unexpected Catastrophe has led to a stalemate, and some breathing room for us.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: The two of you need to get some rest. Especially you, Doctor. You've hardly slept since you've been back, right?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I'm fine...
Theresa glances at Kal'tsit, who seems to sigh wordlessly with her eyes.
The King of Sarkaz senses guilt and restlessness. It is not an easy thing to accept, watching so many Infected turn to dust before one's eyes.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Doctor... do you think all this is your fault?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: It is.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I won't run from my responsibility, and I won't wallow in self-pity... I just need time to accept the present.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I—

a.text: I don't know if Originium is supposed to hurt a newborn civilization like this.
<color=#000000>But Originium is the only way to protect all life and existence.</color>

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You're tired, Doctor. I'm grateful that you have chosen to bear the burden of these emotions for the sake of this great land.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Your pain and struggle shows your kindness and ideals. I won't try to wipe them away, but we could share this burden, if you are willing...
Theresa wants to hold the Doctor's hand, perceive the Doctor's guilt- and anxiety-filled soul.
She wants to help the Doctor.
But a tiny speck of noise echoes ominously in the King's mind.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: (The Doctor is rejecting me? Or is it...?)

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Sorry, Theresa, but this is not something you need to take on.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: No need to use Civilight Eterna on me. It takes a toll on you too. There are more important uses for it.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: More important than helping someone who's given everything for us?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Hehe... thank you. I mean it.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: You and Scout said we have some breathing room, right?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I'll make dinner for us, then. I learned it off Misery.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: For our future challenges.
